name: Washington
source: gun-policy Season 3 Stage 5, Washington hand-overs (wa/HANDOVER-A.md part 7, wa/HANDOVER-B.md item 4, write/wa-01/recipe.json), 2026-11-13
sessions: Two-year sessions that start in odd years.
bill_data: Open States bulk files for 2017 to 2022 (read unchanged as LegiScan-layout folders).
LegiScan for 2023 onward: per-bill calls only; never re-pull a dataset (runner, 2026-11-13).

votes.floor_rule: Floor votes only: "Final Passage" motions with a total of 40 or more. Open States "other" (excused or absent) counts as absent.
gaps: Committee votes before 2023 are mostly missing in Open States.
Conference-committee floor votes needed a tool fix (2026-11-13).

texts.marks: HTML texts: added words are underlined (saved as {+ +}), struck words struck through (saved as [- -]). A "NEW SECTION" is all new law.
texts.note: Text versions carry no dates in this data: each bill is read at one text (the last enrolled, else the last listed), so a vote cannot be tied to its exact text. A PDF-only link has an HTML copy at the same path under /Htm/.

search_note: Washington sponsorships and House and Senate floor votes on this topic come from the bulk bill data (listed above): skip the legislature's sponsor lists and roll-call pages (app.leg.wa.gov), and add the place "sponsor list: covered by bulk bill data". Spend the search on their own words (statements, campaign pages, newsletters, floor remarks, interviews, questionnaires). If any page returns 403, an empty page or a bot check, record it as blocked and move on: do not retry it with a different user agent, headers or tool.
bill_table_note:
- Washington bill text marks changes to existing law (added words underlined, struck words struck through); `operative_text` quotes the law as the bill leaves it. A "NEW SECTION" is all new law.
- One text was read per bill: the last enrolled version, else the last version listed. Text versions carry no dates in this data, so a roll call cannot be tied to the text it was taken on. Where `provenance.note` or the instrument says the version read is not the one passed, say so in `why`, and flag the bill if an earlier text could carry a different rung.
- Most bills here have no floor vote: a roster member sponsored them. Their rung still matters, for sponsors.
quirks: Official roll-call pages print a party label beside each name: never copy from them.
Open States people files use current names, which can differ from the name a member served under.
sponsor cover must match names inside this state's roster only: two matches to namesakes in other states were refused (2026-11-13).
